event_description: Fires when a user transitions from signed-out to signed-in (any provider: Google, email OTP, password, or anonymous).
Fires when the user explicitly signs out of the app.
Fires when the user starts the 30-day account-deletion countdown.
Fires when the user cancels a pending account deletion within its grace period.
Fires when a step of the welcome/onboarding flow is shown. Properties: step (welcome_slides | name | currency | handle | analytics | notify).
Fires when a step of the welcome/onboarding flow is passed (Continue or Skip). Properties: step, same values as onboarding_step_viewed.
Fires once, when OnboardingScreen finishes and the user lands on the main app for the first time. Guarded by the ONBOARDING_COMPLETED_KEY SecureStorage flag so a later re-open never repeats it.
Fires when a user creates a new expense-splitting group. Properties: group_id, member_count (always 1 at creation).
Fires when a user joins an existing group via invite link or token. Properties: group_id.
Fires when a user leaves a group they belong to. Properties: group_id.
Fires when a user adds a non-app member (placeholder) to a group, indicating proxy assignment. Properties: group_id.
Fires when a user answers 'not me' on the unclaimed-name identity prompt. Properties: group_id.

Fires when GroupRepositoryImpl.reconcilePlaceholder merges a placeholder identity onto a real user. Properties: group_id, claim_source (group_join | group_home | group_settings) — see PlaceholderClaimSources.

Occasional (once per group per app session) snapshot of a group's shape, since the PostHog wrapper's group() associates only one current group per user and doesn't fit a member belonging to many groups. Properties: group_id, member_count, expense_count, age_days.
Fires when a user adds a new expense to a group. Properties: split_mode, group_id, entry_method (manual | scan).
Fires when a user edits an existing expense, indicating engagement depth. Properties: group_id.
Fires when a user deletes an expense, a potential churn or correction signal. Properties: group_id.
Fires when a user records a payment to settle outstanding balances, the core value-delivery moment. Properties: group_id.
Fires when a user creates an itemized bill (split-the-bill feature), measuring AI/itemized feature adoption. Properties: item_count, group_id.
Fires when the user answers the up-front 'how are you splitting this?' question. Properties: approach (divide | by_item). The cheapest signal for how much anyone wants the itemized/scan feature.

Fires at the receipt-source picker, before any cost is incurred. Properties: source (photos | files | camera), group_id. The gap between this and scan_started is the 'changed my mind at the picker' rate.
Fires when the picked file(s) are handed to the OCR call. Properties: page_count, source, group_id.
Fires when OCR returns a usable draft. Properties: page_count, item_count, duration_ms, group_id, scan_id (when the server provides one).
Fires when OCR ends without a usable draft (offline, no receipt found, not configured, or a network/server error). Properties: kind, page_count, duration_ms, group_id, scan_id (when present).
Fires when the user cancels a scan mid-flight. Money spent (the round-trip may already be in progress), value zero. Properties: page_count, duration_ms, group_id.
Fires when the server turns a scan away before attempting it (429 per-user rate limit today). Properties: reason, group_id.

Fires when a scanned bill is saved. Properties: items_changed, items_total, group_id. The trust metric: a scan where every line was corrected is a scan that did not work, regardless of the success rate.

Server-side mirror of the receipt_scan_log row for a finished scan (ANALYTICS_PLAN_C_JOURNEY_AND_CLAIMING.md §4). Properties: scan_id, group_id, outcome (ok | not_receipt | invalid_draft | failed | rate_limited | breaker_open), tiers_used (['primary'] or ['primary','escalation']), is_fallback, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_micros, duration_ms. Sent via the HTTP capture endpoint directly (not posthog-node) since a batched SDK can lose events when the edge function's isolate tears down before its next flush; inert with no POSTHOG_API_KEY set.

Web claim flow only. Fires once per ClaimStore instance when the claim link first resolves. No bill-identifying properties: neither BillHeader nor the pre-bill-load resolve responses expose a safe, non-bearer id (the bill token itself is a live credential and must never be sent to an analytics vendor).

Web claim flow. Fires when the resolve response is state=pick_name, i.e. this guest was offered a list of existing unclaimed placeholders before being allowed to type a new name. Properties: candidate_count. The exposure denominator for the anti-duplication design (ANALYTICS_PLAN_C_JOURNEY_AND_CLAIMING.md §5a).

Web claim flow. Fires once the guest's identity is settled, either path. Properties: outcome (claimed_placeholder | created_new), source (pick_name_list | name_entry_suggestion | pick_name_declined | name_entry_direct). pick_name_declined means she saw the candidate list and typed a new name anyway; name_entry_direct means there was never a placeholder to offer her.
Web claim flow. Fires when claimPlaceholder returns won:false — two guests tapped the same placeholder and this one lost the first-claim-wins race.
Web claim flow. Fires from setClaim when quantity > 0 (a claim, not an unclaim). Properties: expense_id, item_id.
Web claim flow. Fires from undoChange. Properties: expense_id.
Web claim flow. Fires from setDone(true) — the guest tapped 'I'm done'. Properties: expense_id, item_count (this guest's own claimed line count).
